title: Karma and rebirth
examples: What is the difference between moksha and nirvana?

explain.say: Karma is a Sanskrit word that means action. Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs all teach that our actions have results that shape our future, in this life and beyond it.
These faiths teach samsara, a cycle of birth, death and rebirth. What we do and intend in one life helps shape the next.
Karma is often compared to planting seeds: kind actions grow good fruit and harmful actions grow painful fruit. In many teachings it is a natural law of cause and effect, not a punishment.

draw.a: Many teachings call it a law of cause and effect

explain.say: The goal is to be freed from the cycle. Hindus and Jains call this freedom moksha, Buddhists call it nirvana, and Sikhs speak of mukti, liberation and union with God.

items: Hinduism | the atman, the eternal self | moksha
Buddhism | no fixed self, a stream of mind | nirvana
Jainism | the jiva, the soul | moksha
Sikhism | the soul | mukti, union with God

explain.say: Each faith sees it a little differently. Buddhists teach there is no unchanging soul, so rebirth is like one candle lighting another. Jains see karma as fine matter sticking to the soul, and Sikhs stress God's grace.

items: Hindu: actions shape the atman's next life
Buddhist: like a flame passed on
Jain: karma as fine matter on the soul
Sikh: grace and remembering God free us

explain.say: Religions such as Judaism, Christianity and Islam mostly teach one earthly life followed by God's judgement, so the idea of rebirth is one of the big differences between traditions.

faq.a: Karma means action. In Hindu, Buddhist, Jain and Sikh teaching, every intentional action has results: kind actions bring good results and harmful ones bring suffering, in this life or a future one.

Reincarnation, or rebirth, is the belief that after death a person is born again in a new body. In Hinduism, Jainism and Sikhism, the soul passes on; Buddhism teaches rebirth without a fixed, unchanging soul.
Samsara is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth. Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs teach that beings are carried round this cycle by karma until they are freed from it.
asks: What is the cycle of rebirth?

faq.q: What is the difference between moksha and nirvana?
faq.a: Both mean freedom from the cycle of rebirth. Moksha is the Hindu and Jain word, often described as the true self being freed or united with the divine. Nirvana is the Buddhist word, meaning the blowing out of craving and suffering.
asks: Is nirvana the same as moksha?

faq.a: In many teachings, no. Karma is described as a natural law of cause and effect, like seeds growing into plants. In some Hindu traditions God oversees karma, but it is still our own actions that shape what happens.

faq.q: Is karma the same as fate?
faq.a: Not quite. Past karma shapes the situation you are born into, but you are free to choose how you act now, and those choices make new karma. So these traditions stress responsibility, not just fate.
asks: Does karma mean everything is decided?

faq.q: What do Buddhists believe is reborn?
faq.a: Buddhists teach anatta, no unchanging self. What continues is a stream of changing mind and karma, often compared to one candle lighting another: the flame passes on, but it is not exactly the same flame.
asks: Do Buddhists believe in a soul?

faq.q: What do Jains believe about karma?
faq.a: Jains see karma as fine, invisible particles that stick to the soul when we act with passion or cause harm. Non-violence, self-discipline and fasting help wear it away until the soul is free and pure.

faq.q: What do Sikhs believe about karma and rebirth?
faq.a: Sikhs believe in karma and rebirth, and that human life is a precious chance to come close to God. Liberation, called mukti, comes through God's grace, remembering God's name and living truthfully and serving others.

faq.q: Can good karma cancel bad karma?
faq.a: Many teachers say good actions do not simply erase harmful ones like a sum, but they create good results and change your habits. Buddhists also stress intention: what you mean to do shapes the karma.
asks: How do you get good karma?

faq.q: Do Christians and Muslims believe in reincarnation?
faq.a: Mainstream Christianity and Islam, like most of Judaism, teach one earthly life, followed by resurrection or judgement by God. Belief in rebirth is mainly found in religions that began in India.
asks: Do Abrahamic religions believe in rebirth?

faq.q: What is the Bhagavad Gita's teaching on rebirth?
faq.a: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that the self is eternal, and that just as a person puts on new clothes and casts off old ones, the self takes on new bodies.
asks: What does the Gita say about death?

faq.q: What is the wheel of life?
faq.a: In Tibetan Buddhist art, the wheel of life shows samsara: beings in different realms, turned by greed, hatred and ignorance, which are shown as a rooster, a snake and a pig at the centre.

facts: Karma is a Sanskrit word meaning action.
Samsara is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth taught in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism.
Liberation from rebirth is called moksha in Hinduism and Jainism, nirvana in Buddhism, and mukti in Sikhism.
Buddhism teaches anatta, that there is no permanent, unchanging self.
Judaism, Christianity and Islam mostly teach one earthly life followed by judgement.

quiz.say: What does the word karma mean?
quiz.why: Karma is Sanskrit for action: our intentional actions and their results.

wrong.0: Karma is not fixed fate; present choices create new karma.
wrong.2: Heaven is a place in many religions, not the meaning of karma.
wrong.3: Prayer is a practice, not what karma means.

quiz.say: A Buddhist helps a stranger with no thought of reward. What do Buddhists say this does?

options.show: Creates good karma, through good intention and action
options.say: Creates good karma, through good intention and action

quiz.why: Buddhists stress intention: a kind act done with a good heart creates good karma.

wrong.0: Buddhists teach that every intentional act has results.
wrong.2: Good karma does not guarantee a particular rebirth like becoming a god.
wrong.3: Meditation is still part of the path.

quiz.say: Which faith would say rebirth happens without an unchanging soul?
quiz.show: Rebirth without an unchanging soul is taught in…
quiz.why: Buddhism teaches anatta, no fixed self; rebirth is like a flame passed from candle to candle.

wrong.0: Hindus speak of the atman, an eternal self, being reborn.
wrong.1: Jains speak of the jiva, the soul, being reborn.
wrong.3: Sikhs speak of the soul being reborn until it is freed.
